# dsh-openpeon
English | 中文
Unofficial client of OpenPeon CESP v1.0; not affiliated with PeonPing. It bundles **no audio** — see
l client of OpenPeon CESP v1.0; not affiliated with PeonPing. It bundles **no audio** — see License.
## Summary
Makes a session audible: when the session's state changes, you hear a sound and see a notification.
- Sounds for six moments: a session starts or ends, the agent starts working or finishes, it fails,

or it needs your input.
- An in-app banner, plus an OS notification if you allow it.
- Sound packs c
ome from the OpenPeon registry: browse and download them on the Plugins page, then listen, switch or
OpenPeon registry: browse and download them on the Plugins page, then listen, switch or delete them.
## Install
This plugin lives outside the DSH checkout, at `~/coding/dsh-plugins/dsh-openpeon`, so the upstream
tree keeps tracking clean. It is a **bundle**: the package ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, so inst
alling it into a profile adds its row to the plugin tree — no hand-written row in the profile's patc
it into a profile adds its row to the plugin tree — no hand-written row in the profile's patch file.
1. Add the package to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json` and list it in `dsh.profile.bundles`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
2. `pnpm install` inside that profile directory, then `pnpm build` here.
The pack ships as `lib/index.js` (host half, Node builtins only) and `lib/client.js` (browser half,
baseline modules only), so nothing here needs to be published or installed next to the DSH sources.
## Use it
Open the **Plugins** page in the sidebar and open **dsh-openpeon** — its configuration sits under th
gins** page in the sidebar and open **dsh-openpeon** — its configuration sits under the description.
1. **Pick a sound pack.** The page lists the packs you have installed and the 370 packs the registry
offers. Search by name, author, tag or language. Each catalogue row shows the pack's author, licens
e, trust tier, size and sound count. *Download* installs one; once installed, *Preview* plays one of
its sounds, *Use* makes it the active pack, and *Delete* removes it. Only what you download is kept

, on your machine.
2. **Choose the moments.** Each of the six rows has two independent switches — **
sound** and **notify** — plus its own *Preview* button. Want the working sound without a popup every
time the agent starts? Arm the sound and leave notify off. Previewing does not wait for the event t

o happen, and it works even while alerts are off.
3. **Silence subagents if you want to.** With *Ign
ore subagent alerts* on, the sessions of delegated subagents neither sound nor notify — the more chi
ldren run at once, the more this matters, since several finishing together is a burst of identical a

lerts.
4. **Turn alerts on** with the switch at the top, and set the volume with the slider. Your ch
oices are remembered in this browser.
Each sound is a CESP v1.0 category, and a pack supplies its audio under those category names. The th
ird column is therefore what a pack has to fill for that sound to play:
| Sound | What sets it off | CESP category |

| Session start | a session appears | `session.start` |
| Working | the agent starts on a turn | `ta

sk.acknowledge` |
| Finished | the turn stops — including when you interrupt it | `task.complete` |

| Failure | the agent hits an error | `task.error` |
| Needs input | an approval or a question is wa

iting for your answer | `input.required` |
| Session end | a session goes away | `session.end` |
A pack need not cover all six — a moment whose category it leaves out simply stays silent, so if one
moment matters to you, check that the pack lists its category before installing.
[该节后续省略]
## Understand the implementation
One bundle (its `cordis.patch.yml` supplies the row) with two sides. The **Host side** runs in the h
arness process and owns the files, the network and the routes; the **Client side** runs in the brows
er and owns the Plugins-page configuration, the banners and playback. The two sides only ever talk o
ver one HTTP prefix, `/openpeon`.
## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
- **Three of the nine standard moments are missing.** `task.progress`, `resource.limit` and `user.sp
am` have no corresponding DSH event, and a switch that can never fire would mislead. Adding one mean

s adding the event that drives it — and the files, since packs are downloaded per moment.
- **The fi
rst launch has no sound.** Installing needs the network, and nothing plays until a pack is chosen. T

he configuration section says so instead of failing silently.
- **Downloads need the CDN.** `github.
com` and `raw.githubusercontent.com` are not used; everything comes from `cdn.jsdelivr.net`. If the
CDN cannot serve a pinned ref, the install fails with an HTTP or digest error rather than installing

something unverified.
- **A "finished" sound also fires when a turn is interrupted.** It rides the

run transition, which also covers a stop; only a dedicated completion event would make it exact.
- *

*Volume is global.** There is no per-moment volume.
- **The subagent filter trusts the Host's marker
.** It recognises a delegated child by `origin: "subagent"` on the `api-session/added` summary. If t
he plugin loads after a subagent has already started and no further summary is published for it, tha

t subagent's later transitions still alert once.
- **The notification body is plain text.** No icon,

tag, or `requireInteraction`; the in-app banner covers the richer presentation.
- **A pack is third
-party content.** The catalogue shows its trust tier, license and automated quality tier before you
install it, but the audio plays as its author made it — a `flagged` quality tier is worth heeding.
